- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak.
- If model forecast is > 10% above recent 7-day average, consider mean reversion bias; reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment strongly supports.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome shows early decline after peak, model often fails to anticipate; add 1–2 days of downward correction.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag; align forecast with sentiment swing midpoint, not peak.
